evidence: Code-path proof: query_data.rs publicly re-exports safe, unsealed QueryDataAccess and QueryMutData with unrestricted Item lifetime type and fetch_mut_with_component_locations(&mut World). A safe downstream implementation may return Some(world) and use no-op access declaration. QueryState::try_new accepts it; empty required/without archetype index matches all actual entities, cache compiles zero bindings, projection succeeds. Public get_many_mut for two distinct live entity IDs passes duplicate and filter/preflight checks, then collect_many_query_items invokes unsafe fetch_mut_from_plans_unchecked twice on the same world pointer and retains both D::Item<world> values. Thus two &mut World aliases escape safe API. Unique iterator and combination array paths share the missing disjoint-borrow constraint. This is distinct from the rejected lending duplicate claim and is static proof, not Cargo execution.
impact: A safe public implementation and safe query call can obtain simultaneously live aliased mutable references to the same World, violating Rust exclusivity.
impact_or_question: A safe public implementation and safe query call can obtain simultaneously live aliased mutable references to the same World, violating Rust exclusivity.
next_action: Product owner must establish the lowest query extraction safety boundary (sealed/unsafe implementation contract or borrow enforcement), audit all multi-item and iterator raw-pointer paths, and add an accepted regression; no API or behavior change in this audit.
